clue.text: People absorbed in local activities

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'People absorbed in local activities' (6) gives SCOTCH by no parse found: no word gives CH or a container, and a search of the exact text found nothing; likely an OCR misread or cut short.

clue.text: It may describe one who has been singularly successful

definitions.text: It may describe one who has been singularly successful

parts.words: It may describe one who has been singularly successful
parts.note: singularly here means all on one's own, so the clue describes someone whose success came without help from anyone else

explanation.definitionFit: A person who rose by their own efforts alone, from humble beginnings, is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Said to be celebrated

explanation.definitionFit: To remark something is to have commented on it, and a festival or anniversary kept with ceremony has likewise been marked in this sense.

clue.text: Sign on the staff

parts.note: staff suggests employees, but it is the musical stave, and the sign is the symbol at its start fixing the pitch of the lines

explanation.definitionFit: The treble or bass symbol written at the left of a musical stave sets which notes its lines stand for.

clue.text: Wrongdoer making final bid to get outside

indicators.note: the bid is told to go around the outside of the word for final, enclosing it

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction
the final part of something is its end

explanation.surface: A criminal makes one last attempt to get out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final bid' reads as one phrase, a last offer, but splits into two pieces, and 'to get outside' makes the second wrap round the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breaks the law or a rule is a culprit, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: His experiment was quick to prove its success

definitions.text: His experiment was quick to prove its success

parts.words: His experiment was quick to prove its success
parts.note: quick is used in its old sense of alive, so the experiment succeeded when the creature it made came to life

explanation.surface: A scientist whose trial gave fast results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' in the old sense means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's novel tells of the scientist who assembled a creature and brought it to life.

clue.text: The right side of the map

definitions.text: The right side of the map

parts.words: The right side of the map
parts.note: maps are normally drawn with north at the top, so the right-hand edge points towards sunrise

explanation.definitionFit: With north at the top, the compass point where the sun rises lies on a map's right-hand edge.

clue.text: It's a strange leader who won't lead

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual order, so the letters of leader are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd sort of leader who declines to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and other card games, the player who distributed the cards does not play first; the player to their left leads.
explanation.definitionFit: At cards the player who hands out the cards is not the one who plays first to the trick.

clue.text: Save cash

explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone from sin is one sense; to exchange a voucher or bond for money is another.

clue.text: Surgeon reveals inclination about retirement

parts.note: a ship's list is its lean or tilt to one side

indicators.note: retirement is a withdrawal or going back, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re is the short word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A doctor admits he is leaning towards stopping work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns RE into ER. Joseph Lister was the Victorian British surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was a pioneering nineteenth-century British doctor who introduced antiseptic operating methods.

clue.text: Bowlers may hang around here, and that's strange

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of 'and that's' are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Cricket bowlers loitering about, which the speaker finds odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowlers are not cricketers but bowler hats, which hang on a hall stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hard round felt hat, and a hall pole with pegs is where hats are hung up.

clue.text: Revealing though unintentional expression of a sinful pride, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words 'a sinful pride' might be arranged some other way, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip that they are proud in a sinful way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A SINFUL PRIDE. The surface's sinful pride is itself the kind of thing such a slip might reveal.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal error thought to betray a hidden wish is named after the father of psychoanalysis.

clue.text: Doctor about to get an increase

definitions.note: the answer as a noun means an extra amount, as in 'some ___'

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is an army doctor
re is the short word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A doctor is about to be given a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is only a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for an extra helping or a larger quantity is asking for an additional amount.

clue.text: A duck for a well-known bowler

explanation.definitionFit: A male duck has this name, and Sir Francis Drake famously finished his game of bowls at Plymouth before facing the Armada.

clue.text: Yield what is sown, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: what a farmer sows in the ground is seed

explanation.surface: A farmer giving up what has been planted, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks a homophone: SEED and CEDE are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up territory or a point in argument is to surrender it.

clue.text: Mother is upset over our love-affair

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, that is above, the second
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for mother is read bottom to top

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother is distressed about our romance.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned bottom to top, and 'over' means placed above the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: French for love, the word is used in English for a romantic, often secret, liaison.

clue.text: In any case, a refusal will not please

definitions.note: a verb phrase meaning to displease or irritate

indicators.note: in tells us the refusal goes inside the next word
case means the word any acts as the container holding the refusal

parts.note: taken as written
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Turning someone down will upset them whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' looks like 'whatever happens' but tells you to put NO in ANY used as a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate or vex someone is the opposite of giving them pleasure.

clue.text: As worn for a sea burial?

definitions.text: As worn for a sea burial?

parts.words: As worn for a sea burial?
parts.note: black clothes are worn when grieving, and a burial at sea takes the body down into the depths

explanation.definitionFit: Full black clothing worn in the first period of grief carries a phrase whose first word also suits ocean depths.

clue.text: Reproduction of a man's oil painting

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, here signalling that the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A print copied from a man's oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction of' rearranges A MAN'S OIL, with the S of the apostrophe counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait of a smiling woman in the Louvre is the most famous picture in the world.

clue.text: Solid block of cars

parts.note: a solid suggests a mass of parked vehicles, but here it is the geometric solid, and the block is the part of a car engine housing the pistons

explanation.definitionFit: It is a geometric solid with circular ends, and engines are built around a block of these chambers in which pistons move.

clue.text: Discount only? Free? Here, everything comes off!

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters of 'discount only' are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop advertising nothing but discounts and freebies, where everything is marked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything comes off' reads as price cuts, matching 'discount', but means clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist community is a place where people go about without any clothes at all.

clue.text: A quick grasp of music

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden grab is one meaning; a short fragment of a song or tune heard briefly is the other.

clue.text: He puts up the points or puts them down

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the player who makes goals or runs; the other is the official who records the tally.

clue.text: Cut a prison term

explanation.definitionFit: A small notch is one sense; in British slang the same word means jail or a police station.

clue.text: Forger's block

parts.note: a forger suggests a counterfeiter, but here it is someone who works at a forge, hammering metal on an iron block

explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith shapes hot metal by hammering it on this heavy iron block.

clue.text: Bail out in the Indian Ocean

indicators.note: out means out of order or disordered, so the letters of bail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bailing water out of a boat at sea in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BAIL. The definition describes the island by its location.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian holiday island east of Java lies on the edge of that ocean.

clue.text: A spinner at his peak?

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A spin bowler at the height of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler but is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means on the summit or uppermost point of something.

clue.text: Some light or heavy timber

explanation.definitionFit: A ray or shaft of light is one sense; a large structural length of wood is the other.

clue.text: Accelerator or choke

explanation.definitionFit: The valve controlling an engine's fuel flow is one sense; to strangle someone is the other.

clue.text: Indeed upset when refused

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of indeed are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is truly put out at being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be turned down or have a request rejected is to be declined.

clue.text: Dance band pieces

parts.note: a horn is an instrument played in a band
a pipe is also an instrument played in a band

explanation.surface: Musicians in a band playing dance numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band pieces' looks like tunes but supplies two instruments in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively solo jig traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: I'm not one to weaken

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
a pair is two, which is not one

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are no weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'I'm not one to give in', but 'not one' means two.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or reduce the strength or quality of something.
